summary_hint: employer, employee, pay period, gross pay, YTD gross

typed_core.name: employer_address
typed_core.why: IN-5 disambiguator — two employers with similar names are distinguished by address

typed_core.name: employee_name
typed_core.why: ID-1 — name consistency across the file

typed_core.name: employee_address
typed_core.why: ID-4 — currently reachable only via the catch-all, so ID-4 gets NOTHING from a pay stub today

typed_core.name: employee_ssn_masked
typed_core.why: PII protection — many stubs print a partial SSN, which today lands UNMASKED in the catch-all. Typing it is the only way to keep it out
typed_core.prompt_hint: Last 4 only. NEVER place an SSN in additional_sections

typed_core.name: position_or_title
typed_core.why: IN-7 — 'is the new role the same field'. Nothing else on a pay stub carries the job title
typed_core.prompt_hint: Often near the employee name or in a header block. Null if absent — do NOT infer from the employer's industry

typed_core.name: pay_date
typed_core.why: IN-2 — 'the most recent pay date; compare age to the window'

typed_core.name: pay_frequency
typed_core.why: IN-3 — periods elapsed depends on it; IN-1 annualisation
typed_core.prompt_hint: Infer from the period dates when not stated; record the reasoning in the snippet

typed_core.name: net_pay
typed_core.why: FR-1 — gross minus deductions must equal net; an arithmetic break is the alteration signal

typed_core.name: total_deductions_current
typed_core.why: FR-1 — the middle term of the reconciliation

nested_lists.name: earnings_lines
nested_lists.shape_reason: 3-8 lines; flat rows are trivially cheap and generalise better than four named YTD fields

fields.name: earning_type
fields.why: IN-11 — regular / overtime / bonus / commission. THE KEY FIELD: IN-10 and IN-11 both turn on separating base from variable income, and a single ytd_gross cannot express it

fields.name: ytd_amount
fields.why: IN-10, IN-11 — Priya's B12 case (base declined while bonus rose) turns on this split

fields.name: label
fields.why: FR-4 — 'deduction lines implying an obligation'. A garnishment appears as GARN / Levy / Child Supp / Wage Attach

fields.name: category
fields.why: FR-4 — tax / benefit / garnishment / retirement / other

rejected.name: four named YTD fields (ytd_regular / ytd_overtime / ytd_bonus / ytd_commission)
rejected.reason: superseded by the earnings_lines list — same information, generalises to arbitrary earnings types, and one list costs the same ~5 sites as none of the four would

rejected.name: check_number / direct_deposit_account
rejected.reason: no consumer; account detail is PII with no rule need

rejected.name: filing_status / allowances
rejected.reason: tax detail; no rule reads it

rejected.name: employer_ein
rejected.reason: the W-2 carries it; a stub rarely does

rejected.name: income_is_stable
rejected.reason: a judgment, not a fact — IN-10/IN-11's job. Tags describe; rules judge

rejected.name: is_garnishment_present
rejected.reason: a judgment — FR-4 interprets the deduction lines

encoding_variations: Every payroll provider differs — ADP, Paychex, Gusto, Workday, in-house
YTD components may be a column beside current amounts, a separate YTD block, or absent
Pay frequency is often implied by the period dates rather than stated
Deduction labels vary: garnishments appear as GARN, Levy, Child Supp, Wage Attach

open_questions.q: earnings_lines list vs four named YTD fields
open_questions.recommendation: the list — it generalises to arbitrary earnings types and costs the same ~5 sites

options: instruct the prompt to omit entirely
open_questions.recommendation: typed masked field — no rule needs it, but typing it is the ONLY way to keep it out of the unmasked catch-all
include, but MEASURE — IN-7 scores 100% on a fixture where occupation is always present; on real stubs it may often be null, pushing IN-7 to unknown

notes: The shipping extractor has 11 typed-core fields, all with consumers — nothing to remove. This spec adds 6 fields and 2 nested lists.

The earnings_lines list is the most valuable addition: IN-10 and IN-11 both require separating base from variable income, which a single ytd_gross cannot express. Priya's B12 case (base declined, bonus rose, total flat) is exactly this.
